title: Alexa Routine Execution Delay
app: Home Assistant, Matter and Thread border routers, Alexa routine logs, Google Home automations, Zigbee2MQTT bridges, SmartThings, Node-RED, and webhooks streamed to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=alexa:routine
| stats avg(execution_delay_ms) as avg_delay_ms, max(execution_delay_ms) as max_delay_ms by routine_name
| where avg_delay_ms>3000 OR max_delay_ms>10000
| sort - avg_delay_ms
description: Uses Alexa routine logs telemetry to monitor delay between trigger and routine completion in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for routines that feel slow or flaky in real life, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Alexa routine logs data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a hourly cadence.
visualization: Routine table of average and peak execution delay.
grandmaExplanation: It flags delay between trigger and routine completion so you can spot routines that feel slow or flaky in real life before it becomes annoying.
